references.text: Isaiah prophesies that the Lord's servant will be 'taken away' from the living – this points forward to the bridegroom who is taken away from the disciples.
The parallel passage in Matthew where Jesus uses the same image of the bridegroom being taken away, and that the disciples should then fast.
The parallel passage in Mark where Jesus speaks about the bridegroom being taken away from the wedding guests, and then they should fast.
The preceding verse where Jesus asks if the wedding guests can fast while the bridegroom is with them – which provides the context for verse 35.
John the Baptist refers to Jesus as the bridegroom and himself as the friend of the bridegroom – the same bridegroom metaphor found in Luke 5:35.
After Jesus was taken away (the ascension), the disciples fasted and prayed in the early church – a fulfillment of Jesus' words that they should fast when the bridegroom is taken from them.
The early church practiced fasting and prayer, in accordance with Jesus' prophecy that the disciples should fast after he was taken from them.
The bride (the church) and the bridegroom (Christ) are finally united – the image of the bridegroom that Jesus uses in Luke 5:35 finds its ultimate fulfillment.
